notes: Only 35 of the 100 shortlisted papers fit: the search terms pulled in many single-species GRN and single-cell atlases plus disease studies, which the definition excludes, so the keep list is short of 50 rather than padded. The kept set covers de novo gene origin (Drosophila, human, E. coli), whole-genome duplication and duplicate-gene fates (sturgeon, gastropods, cotton, soybean, tea, citrus, horse chestnut, wheat), cis-regulatory evolution (C3/C4 grasses, plant stem-cell regulator, mouse, human-chimp), Hox and body-plan evolution, morphological novelty and co-option (gliding membranes, bipedalism, deceptive flowers), convergent evolution and comparative genomes (hornworts, ferns, MHC, chromatin loops). It lacks cross-species single-cell developmental atlases, deep-animal GRN comparisons (e.g. cnidarian/sponge), and evo-devo of the vertebrate head or neural crest.
